catalog_quote: [Edgar 1989, 3.0 TONE] According to the evidence to date the languages of the Maba group would appear to have at least two phonemic tones. This seems to be true for Masalit (high tone, low tone, falling tone, rising tone and downsteps are present). ... Some minimal pairs: ... kara bed / kara girl ... [tone marks lost in scanned] ... From the small amount of evidence at hand it appears that tone plays a morphologically and lexically significant role: - In nominal singular/plural distinction: in general singular nominals are characterized by a final low tone, plurals by a final high. - Cardinal numbers are characterized by the tone patterns (L)H or (H)H ... [SIL 2011, sect. 5] Tone, stress and vowel length all play a role in the Massalit language. The system is complex and our studies to this point have not yielded satisfactory results. audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both cited passages (Edgar 1989 p. 13 sect. 3.0 TONE; SIL 2011 sect. 5 pp. 7-8) are verbatim in the copies we hold at the stated locators. (2) The classification 'tonal, no stress rule stated' rests on the only published grammar of the language (Edgar 1989, grammar sketch, 121 pp; complete phonology chapter held) and the SIL Chad orthography statement (2011), which explicitly says tone, stress and length all play a role but the system is unanalyzed. Web search (Glottolog 5.3, SIL archive hits, ELA page, lingref, masarak.org/kanamasaraka, archive.org Rosetta items) found no instrumental study, JIPA illustration, dissertation or phonology article on Masalit prosody; Leffel 2012 (downloaded, p. 221 fn. 3) independently confirms 'No complete analysis of the Masalit tonal system exists'. The other Rosetta excerpts of Edgar 1989 and the 2021 SIL Tchad community grammar (downloaded) are silent.

sources.quote: 'Tone is transcribed throughout on the basis of qualitative inspection of f0 contours. ... No complete analysis of the Masalit tonal system exists; unexpected tonal alternations may be due to intonation. See Mathes 2010 for a recent analysis of lexical tone and tone sandhi in Masalit nouns.' Nothing on stress.
